title: Koch Foundation Challenges Cannabis Prohibition From The Right

content_html_sanitized:
The excellent website, MarijuanaMoment.net is reporting Top Conservative Group Urges Supreme Court To Take Marijuana Case Challenging Federal Prohibition.

 

As the article explains, the challenge is being led by  Americans for Prosperity Foundation which is  the “political advocacy group” for the multi billionaire Koch family.

 

Unlike most of the other think tanks, it doesn’t have to worry about keeping outside donors happy, and unlike most of the so-called “conservative” organizations, the Koch family has strong libertarian tendencies.

 

I have been enormously frustrated that many “conservative” organizations, with some notable exceptions, like National Review, have let themselves be captured by the intellectual sleaze of the reefer madness crowd. The Heritage Foundation is an absolute embarrassment.

See

Heritage and Harvard and the War on Truth and Freedom

And links

 

Of course, other anti Prohibitionists also include the Cato Institute, of which Charles Koch was a cofounder. Cato’s executive vice president, the late David Boaz, served on the NORML board of directors when I was National Director.

 

I especially like the Reason Foundation, which also publishes Reason. They have also had support from the Koch family and are explicitly Libertarian and have always been consistently anti Prohibitionist.

 

While the Supreme Court challenge will be about the Constitution, in the background, the political influence of the Koch family will complicate the politics on the Right.

 

The manner in which the ban on “intoxicating hemp” was rammed through Congress offended many on the Right.

See

What The Hemp Ban Reveals About The Condition of Our Democracy
